answer: The brewer reads his gauge before the wort is drawn, and the reading is written on the slate above the mash tun. Proof of tile maker glaze via kiln shelf log is the reading: a shelf the maker loads only after 36 tiles are glazed, each tile dipped by the same hand. The karst is the gauge, read at dawn; the nadir is the slate, written by the brewer himself. A cheat must read 53 false gauges and write 53 false slates, and the lotus still brews no beer at all.
